purpose: Test a separate context-needed boolean, routing only flagged candidates to a wider-context second call, with and without first-pass neighbors, on 10 development papers.
selection: Same ten arXiv development papers as the previous pilot. Nine papers each use one request; the last is divided into two matched candidate groups. 682 original fine-tuned NLI candidates.
first_prompt:
You are reading sentences from scientific papers. Judge each sentence: does it genuinely state a research gap?

The input is sentences from scientific papers, in reading order, one per line as "[id] sentence". Judge every sentence on its own.

Decision — answer YES (keep) if the sentence states ANY of:
  (a) a limitation / weakness / caveat / bias / constraint / assumption of the authors' OWN work (e.g., small sample, no blinding, single setting, short follow-up, confounding, limited generalizability, unvalidated measure, "we did not / could not ...", "a limitation is ...");
  (b) an explicit FUTURE-WORK direction the authors propose ("in future work we will ...", "future research should ...", "it would be interesting to ...");
  (c) an unsolved problem / missing capability / open research gap in the field or prior work ("it remains unknown ...", "no existing method ...", "current approaches struggle with ...").

Answer NO (drop) if the sentence is instead: a result or finding, a method/experimental-setup description, a positive or contribution claim ("we propose/show/achieve ..."), background or related-work description, a citation or reference fragment, acknowledgements / funding / author contributions / competing interests, a figure or table caption, a dataset/metric definition, or a generic non-gap statement.

Judge each sentence on the rules above, without favouring YES or NO.

Return JSON {"results":[{"id":<id>,"keep":<bool>,"needs_more_context":<bool>}, ...]} with exactly one entry for every numbered target. Give your best provisional keep/drop decision in "keep". Independently, set "needs_more_context" to true when you need additional original surrounding text for a reliable decision, even if you have a tentative guess. Mark true when a reference such as "this", "these", "it" or "the method" hides what is limited or when the target could reasonably be a gap or an ordinary observation depending on its context. Otherwise mark false. Only numbered targets are classified; unnumbered neighbors are context.

There is one paper below. Lines starting "PAPER " are boundaries, not sentences. Judge each numbered sentence only in its own paper.

followup: Only flagged numbered targets; up to 3 previous and 3 following original sentences, each <=800 characters. Second-pass boolean overrides first-pass provisional keep.
reuse: Two-paper flag probe responses reused after matching input and prompt; saved single-paper GPU0 one-pass baselines reused for first nine papers after exact input and prompt verification. Last paper split into two groups so baselines rerun.
note: Flag scheme was proposed after tri-state uncertainty produced zero unsure and after seeing a two-paper probe with zero flags; results are exploratory and those papers are not a holdout. No new test data.
labels: LLM-generated, previously studied, not human adjudicated. Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 GPU0, vLLM 0.32.0, same revision and deterministic settings as GPU0 baselines. GPU1 service not used.
